claims.text: The baseline refractory high-entropy alloy has a single-phase, disordered microstructure.
The baseline alloy has balanced room-temperature mechanical properties.
Mechanical alloying followed by consolidation can incorporate a uniform nanoscale Y2O3 dispersion into the alloy.
Temperatures of approximately 700–900°C are relevant to the intended jet-turbine service conditions.
The intervention produces nanoscale Y2O3 particles embedded uniformly in the alloy matrix.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles act as pinning points for dislocations.
Dispersed oxide nanoparticles stabilize grain boundaries.
Dislocation pinning and grain-boundary stabilization slow high-temperature deformation and creep.
The oxide dispersion will not appreciably affect the alloy density.
The oxide dispersion will not appreciably impair room-temperature ductility.
ODS treatment will increase high-temperature creep strength by approximately 20% relative to an otherwise comparable alloy without oxide nanoparticles.
ODS treatment will retain approximately similar room-temperature yield strength relative to the baseline.
ODS treatment will retain approximately similar room-temperature ductility relative to the baseline.
ODS treatment will have only a minimal effect on overall alloy density.
The high-temperature benefit depends on achieving a uniform and optimized nanoparticle distribution.
Excessive particle agglomeration or coarsening may negate the high-temperature benefit.
The proposed benefit may not persist at temperatures substantially outside the tested 700–900°C range.
